objectives: Keep the drain system below the insertion site, upright and sealed with adequate water.
Check and document drainage, swinging and bubbling on a dedicated observation chart.
Know when drainage or suction must not proceed without specialist or prescriber instructions.
Escalate chest pain, persistent cough or worsening breathlessness.

items.text: The decision to insert, drain, suction or remove a chest drain is a medical or specialist decision; follow the inserting team's written instructions.
Keep the drain bottle below the insertion site at all times and keep the drain upright at all times.
The system must contain adequate water to cover the end of the tube.
Use aseptic non-touch technique when changing a drain bottle, underwater-seal drain or drain tubing.
Avoid clamping a bubbling chest tube unless under specialist pleural supervision and in specific circumstances only.

Drainage of a large pleural effusion should be controlled to prevent re-expansion pulmonary oedema; a drain placed for effusion should be clamped promptly in a patient with repetitive coughing or chest pain, because re-expansion pulmonary oedema is potentially fatal.

Avoid suction soon after insertion; suction pressures should be prescribed or documented by the medical team before suction starts, with the unit using one consistent unit of pressure; routine thoracic suction should be avoided given a lack of data showing benefit.
Instructions on clamping and the rate of fluid drainage must be given and recorded, and the volume to drain over a specified period should be stated in the procedure report and handover.

Insertion, suction prescription and decisions about clamping are medical or specialist responsibilities; nursing responsibilities are observation, maintenance of the system as above, documentation and escalation. The source is a UK adult secondary-care clinical statement, not an ICU nursing standard.
Drain type (bottle, digital, ambulatory) and suction equipment follow the unit's supplies and the manufacturer's instructions.
Check the drain daily for wound infection, fluid drainage volume and the presence of respiratory swinging and/or bubbling, and document them on a dedicated chest drain observation chart.
A follow-up chest radiograph within a few hours of insertion checks drain position (a team decision).
Record drainage volume over time, swinging and bubbling, and the patient's breathing, pain and cough.
Report chest pain, persistent cough, worsening breathlessness, new or increased bubbling, drain displacement or disconnection promptly, and do not clamp without instruction.
Re-expansion pulmonary oedema, drain fall-out (hence the holding suture), infection at the wound.
Use the dedicated observation chart for drainage volumes, swinging and bubbling, and record clamping and suction instructions.
Bottle changes, suction connection, troubleshooting a blocked or leaking system and drain removal follow the unit's approved procedure; the practice points read do not give the steps.

checklist.text: Confirm the written instructions for this drain (clamping, rate of drainage, suction) before any care.
Check the drain system is below the insertion site, upright, sealed and has adequate water.
Check the wound, the drainage volume and swinging or bubbling, and record them on the observation chart.
Use aseptic non-touch technique when changing the bottle or tubing.
Do not clamp a bubbling drain and do not start or change suction without instruction.
Report chest pain, persistent cough, worsening breathlessness or a displaced or disconnected drain at once.
Record drainage, swinging, bubbling and instructions given.
